metadata.title: Random But True: The Seal The Internet Might Love To Death
metadata.caption:
Neil is a southern elephant seal, born on Tasmania's Tasman Peninsula in 2020. He weighs about a tonne, and twice a year he hauls himself out of the ocean and straight into Tasmanian coastal towns.

He blocks roads. He rams parked cars. He knocks over road posts and falls asleep in the middle of the street. He has more than 1.5 million followers online and a fan group over 50,000 people deep.

But Tasmania's wildlife officials aren't worried about the cars. They're worried about the crowds - the rules are to stay 20 metres back, and 50 metres if you have a dog with you.

Here's why. In 2022, Norway had Freya, a 1,300-pound walrus who drew the exact same kind of crowds in Oslo Fjord. Despite repeated official warnings, people swam with her, posed for photos, and some threw things at her. On August 14, 2022, Norwegian authorities euthanised her - not because she had injured anyone, but because they concluded the public would never keep its distance.

Officials have a phrase for it: loving an animal to death.
